Kept in the file as a comment above it.
This comment heads the items under it; changing it changes their heading.

Used in %d places: take it out of them first, then delete it.

resources.string: Give it a name the server takes first.
Headscale does not support these: the server will refuse the policy while it has them.
A tag name starts with a letter
Lowercase letters, digits and dashes only
Letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores; not an address
Letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores only
Not an IP address or network: 100.64.0.20, 192.168.1.0/24, fd7a:115c:a1e0::1
The prefix length is out of range: 0–32 for IPv4, 0–128 for IPv6
A group names a set of users, so a rule can say group:admins instead of listing people. A user\'s tagged devices belong to their tags, not to the user\'s groups.
Groups name sets of users, to use in rules
Pick a group to see and change it
Users by login, picked from the tailnet\'s list; a login it does not show yet can be typed.
No members yet: rules that use the group reach no one.
Devices the members own and have not tagged: what a rule with this group as its source covers.
The members have no untagged devices
A tag names a role of devices: rules reach tag:server rather than somebody\'s devices. Its owners are who may put the tag on a device.
Tags name roles of devices and say who may assign them
Pick a tag to see and change it
Who may assign this tag to a device: users, groups, other tags, Admins.
No owners: only admins can assign it.

resources.string: The server refuses rules that use a tag missing from tag owners, and no one can assign it. Add it with Admins as owners, then change them if you like.
The server refuses rules that use a tag missing from tag owners. Add it, then pick who may assign it.
A host gives an address a name: a rule can reach nas:443 instead of 100.64.0.20:443. An IP set gathers addresses, networks, ranges and hosts under one name.
Pick a host or an IP set to see and change it
Hosts name addresses, to use in rules
An IP address or a network: 100.64.0.20, 192.168.1.0/24, fd7a:115c:a1e0::1
No device of the tailnet has this address
Give it a name and an address first.
Addresses, networks, ranges, hosts and other sets, added and taken out in order; rules use the set as ipset:name.
Applied top to bottom: a later row can take out part of what an earlier one added.
Address, range, network, host:name or ipset:name
Give it a name and a first address first.
Routes, exit nodes and services that devices advertise wait for an admin to approve them; these devices skip the wait.
Pick an approval to see and change it
Devices of these users and groups, and devices with these tags.
No one: an admin approves it by hand.
Pick who it is approved for first.
Every route waits for an admin
The network, with its prefix length: 192.168.1.0/24. A device advertising it, or a part of it, is approved.
Enter the route and pick who it is approved for first.
A device offering itself as an exit node is approved at once when it qualifies.
Every exit node waits for an admin
Exit nodes wait for an admin again
Every service host waits for an admin
Devices that may host this Tailscale Service without an admin approving each.
Give the service a name and pick who it is approved for first.
Device attributes turn features on for chosen devices: Funnel, Taildrive, Mullvad, a NextDNS profile. Rules add up; their order does not matter.
Device attributes turn on features such as Funnel and Taildrive for chosen devices
Pick a rule to see and change it
Pick the devices and at least one attribute; nothing is written before both are set.
Written as they are: cap: names and attributes this editor does not explain.
One attribute, without spaces or quotes
Application capabilities and IP pools stay as written; edit them in the JSON editor.
Also %s, which only the server can tell.
These devices may publish a service to the public internet with Funnel. Headscale has no Funnel.
These devices may share folders with Taildrive. Who may open the shares is a grant of the drive capability.
These devices may open folders others share with Taildrive.
These devices may use Mullvad\'s exit nodes. Needs the Mullvad add-on on the tailnet.
A random UDP port instead of 41641, for firewalls that mishandle many devices on one port. Replaces the policy-wide randomizeClientPort.
These devices get no 100.x address, only their Tailscale IPv6 one.
The client stops looking for sign-in pages of hotel and airport Wi-Fi.
MagicDNS answers with the devices\' IPv6 addresses (AAAA records) too.
Device names and models are not sent to NextDNS.
These devices use this NextDNS profile, with NextDNS as the tailnet\'s resolver.
These devices use this Control D profile, with Control D as the tailnet\'s resolver.
A posture lists conditions a device must meet — its OS, client version, security software — before rules that require it let the device through.
Postures set conditions devices must meet before rules let them in
Pick a posture to see and change it
One per row, all must hold: node:os == \'macos\', node:tsVersion >= \'1.80\', node:tsReleaseTrack == \'stable\'. The server checks the syntax.
Write the condition, or remove the row
When a device fails it: %s. Edit in JSON.
Give it a name and a first condition first.
Required by every access rule that names no posture of its own.
None: rules without a posture of their own let every device through.
